messages:
alex: FYI — Acme reported repeated 429s + p95 token latency spikes on their Dedicated pool (eu2) starting ~03:05 UTC. They said it coincided with a model compile. Attaching short traces and repro notes. @maria can you take a look?

alex: ```
RequestIDs: r-acme-01 .. r-acme-37
03:05:12 GPU0 sm% 96, mem% 68
03:05:13 MIG[1g.5gb] slice0 sm% 94, kv_cache_misses spike -> 12k/s
03:05:14 NVML: nvlink bw nominal, l3 read lat spiked
Router logs: 429 ThrottleQueueExceeded for route /v1/generate (pool-eu2)
```

maria: thanks. Quick question — did you try to repro with the customer's request shape or use our standard rps test?

alex: repro steps I used (staging with same model build + MIG config):
1) curl -s -N -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" -d '{"prompt":"<short 16-token>","max_tokens":16}' "https://staging.api.redwood/v1/generate" &
2) concurrency 200 (wrk2), interval burst pattern 10s on / 20s off
Result: p95 tokens jumps from 160ms -> 2.2s, and router starts returning 429 after 60s. GPU traces show repeated kvcache invalidation and SM saturation.

jinx: initial hypothesis: KV cache thrash + fractional MIG packing makes small-request bursts expensive. When a co-located tenant triggers a model compile it drives SM usage high and pushes shared MIG slices into neighbor interference. Two mitigations to try:
- short-term: bump pool-eu2 min_replicas by +1 or route acme to pool-eu2-spare
- short-term: whitelist acme for "cache-pin" so their active KV caches are honored (avoids thrash)
- mid-term: add a compile-quarantine window (compile on dedicated coordinator host or rate-limit compiles)

sam: I pulled node telemetry. There's a matching large compile from tenant "flaky-internal" at 03:02 that pushed one node's SM% to 98% for ~90s. Autoscaler did trigger (+1) at 03:06 but the new pod wasn't Ready until 03:10 -> backlog and router queue grew -> 429s. NVLINK and L3 latencies show slight degradation but not catastrophic. This looks like co-residency + compile time spike.

autoscaler-bot: [alert] pool-eu2 autoscale event: scale_up=+1 at 03:06:14, new instance id i-zzzz ready at 03:10:08, duration 3m54s. backlog_peak=420 requests

maria: immediate actions proposed:
- migrate Acme to spare pool (one-off) or bump min_replicas while we triage
- throttle compile jobs from lower-priority tenants during peak hours
- short-term set router fallback to a lower-capacity model when queue depth > X

alex: executed migrate: `redctl migrate-tenant --tenant acme --from pool-eu2 --to pool-eu2-spare` at 03:12. Post-migrate p95 dropped from 2.1s -> 180ms within two minutes. Customer confirmed improvement. :thumbsup:

jinx: for follow-up RFC: propose a reserved "compile coordinator" pool and a policy to prevent simultaneous heavy compiles on co-located slices. Also consider keeping 1 hot spare slice per dedicated pool to absorb transient compile storms. I'll open infra ticket.

maria: please log an incident note and include the repro script + NVML traces. If Acme escalates, we have the mitigation steps documented. Good catch, alex. :+1:

alex: filing the incident doc and attaching the reproduction script and smutil traces. Will ping when RFC lands.

sam: fyi — created a temporary rule to pause non-prod compiles on that node cluster for the next 24h.

jinx: adding todo: postmortem, autoscaler tuning, compile-quarantine RFC.

maria: closing loop for now. Keep updates in this thread if anything else crops up. :thinking:
